q: In an n-type semiconductor, the majority charge carriers are
why: Pentavalent donor impurities contribute extra free electrons, making electrons the majority carriers.

q: A p-type semiconductor is formed by doping silicon with
why: Trivalent (acceptor) impurities like boron create holes, giving a p-type semiconductor.

q: In forward biasing of a p-n junction, the positive terminal of the battery is connected to the
why: Forward bias connects positive terminal to p-side, reducing the barrier potential and allowing current flow.

q: In reverse bias, the width of the depletion region of a p-n junction
why: Reverse bias widens the depletion region, increasing resistance and allowing only tiny leakage current.

q: A full-wave rectifier using a centre-tapped transformer and two diodes produces output pulses at a frequency (compared to 50 Hz AC input) of
why: Full-wave rectification uses both half cycles, doubling the output pulse frequency to 100 Hz.

q: A Zener diode used for voltage regulation is operated in
why: Zener diodes regulate voltage by operating in reverse breakdown, where voltage stays nearly constant.

q: In a transistor's active (normal) operation, the biasing condition is
why: Normal active-mode transistor operation requires emitter-base forward bias and collector-base reverse bias.

q: For a transistor in CE configuration, if IB = 0.1 mA and current gain beta = 100, the collector current IC is
why: IC = beta x IB = 100 x 0.1 mA = 10 mA.

q: The output of a logic AND gate is 1 only when
why: AND gate: Y = A.B, output is 1 only when every input is 1.

q: Which logic gate is called a 'universal gate' because any other gate can be built using only it?
why: NAND (and also NOR) gates are universal gates, able to construct all other basic logic gates.
